entries.title: Mark selected rows as done without printing a barcode sheet
entries.summary: Both manual lists now have a Mark selected as done button beside Barcode selected. Use it to clear rows you have already handled, without printing a sheet.
watchFor: The rows go straight to Work area assigned, so there is no printed sheet to tick off afterwards.
A confirm panel opens first, so a mis-click on its own clears nothing.
howToSee: Load today's Inbound and Van Scans report
Tick two rows in Needs Manual Review
Click Mark selected as done and read the confirm panel
Confirm, and the rows move to Work area assigned

entries.title: Station tab pulls station packages out of Needs Review
entries.summary: Packages addressed to the station itself now leave Needs Manual Review and get their own Station tab under Set aside. They also stop counting against the progress line.
watchFor: Only packages with the station zip 85027 can match the station. A same-numbered street anywhere else never will.
The list of other names for the station starts empty on purpose, so nothing matches by guesswork.
On a sort that runs past midnight the packages count to the sort day, not to the clock on the wall.
howToSee: Load today's Inbound and Van Scans report
Open Set aside and click Station
Check Needs Manual Review: none of those tracking numbers is in it
The progress line no longer counts them either

entries.title: The Station tab remembers the day: delivered, carry-overs and four counts
entries.summary: The Station tab now remembers the packages it saw earlier in the day. The header counts total, delivered, still needing and coded, and a package carried over from a previous day shows how old it is.
watchFor: Delivered is worked out fresh from each report, never saved. A package that turns up again counts as still out.
Overnight the delivered ones drop off and the ones still needing a scan carry over.
howToSee: Load today's Inbound and Van Scans report
Open Set aside then Station and read the four counts in the header
Load a later Post Sort report that no longer lists one of those packages
That row shows as delivered and the counts move by exactly one

entries.title: Not ours, To Station, Park and Undo on a package
entries.summary: Station and Needs Review rows get four buttons: Not ours, To Station, Park and Undo. Your choice sticks to that tracking number, so the next report does not undo it.
watchFor: Not ours also clears the package from the day, so it cannot come back as a carry-over.
To Station on a parked row releases the park.
A package you marked still open goes back to normal once a Post Sort report lists it again.
howToSee: Load today's Inbound and Van Scans report
Open Set aside then Station and click Not ours on a row
It is back in Needs Manual Review and the Station badge drops by one
Click To Station on a Needs Review row and it stays in Station on the next report

entries.title: Publishing the tool works from the Windows machine too
entries.summary: The scripts that publish the tool to the staging and cage PC sites now run on the Windows machine as well as the Mac. Nothing inside the tool changed.
watchFor: There is nothing to see on screen. If you are hunting for a difference in the tool, there is not one.
howToSee: This one is about publishing, not about the tool
Publishing from the Windows machine now finishes instead of stopping with an error
What gets published is the same either way

entries.title: Copy the Station list for Teams, and edit the station settings
entries.summary: A Copy button on the Station tab puts the packages still needing a scan on the clipboard as plain Teams text. Settings gains fields for the other station names, the station route and the closing line.
watchFor: The button is only on a supervisor device. An admin machine does not get it.
The text is deliberately plain, because Teams turns a pasted dash into a bullet list.
It copies exactly the packages the Station badge counts, no more and no fewer.
howToSee: Load today's Inbound and Van Scans report on a supervisor device
Open Set aside then Station and click Copy
Paste into Teams and read the list and the closing line
Change the closing line in Settings, save, and copy again

entries.title: Address Catcher leaves station packages out of the report
entries.summary: Address Catcher now drops station packages the moment it reads the report, so one cannot turn up in a band, the worklist, an advisory, a misroute flag or an area suggestion.
watchFor: The record count comes out a few rows short of the scan count. That gap is the station packages and it is expected.
With the station settings missing, nothing is dropped at all. It would rather show you too much than hide a real bad address.
Sending a package to Station in the coder also drops it here the next time you load the report.
howToSee: Open Address Catcher and load today's Inbound and Van Scans report
The record count is short by the number of station packages
Look for a station tracking number in the bands: it is not there
Send a row to Station in the coder, reload the report here, and that row is gone too

entries.title: Station rows and your choices ride along in the Day Export
entries.summary: The Day Export file now carries the Station list and your Not ours, To Station and Park choices, so the Cage A admin sees the same Station tab you do.
watchFor: An import adds to what is already on the other device. It never wipes what is there.
A package you parked or marked still open is not marked delivered by an import.
Anything the import refuses is named in the import summary rather than dropped quietly.
howToSee: Load today's report and click Not ours on one station row
Export the day file from the 999 Desk panel
Import it on the other device and open Set aside then Station
The same rows and the same choices are there, and the summary names both lists

entries.title: A list of what is on staging and not yet in production
entries.summary: The list behind this drawer. Every merged change that has not reached the cage PC yet gets one entry, and a check stops a change from going out without one.
watchFor: A change merged minutes ago can show no merge date until the list is rebuilt.
howToSee: Open this drawer: everything you are reading comes from that list
Each card links to the change it describes
The list is published with the build, so it is never older than the page you are on

entries.title: The Release queue: a pinned issue you tick to choose what ships next
entries.summary: A pinned Release queue issue lists the same changes with a checkbox each. Tick the ones you want on the cage PC and a script works out how to ship them.
watchFor: Ticking from the top down is the cheap path. Ticking out of order means pulling changes apart one at a time, which costs another round of review.
Nothing ships because it is ticked. Someone still has to publish.
A tick follows the change it is on, so the list reordering cannot move your tick onto something else.
howToSee: Open the pinned Release queue issue linked at the top of this drawer
Tick the top two changes and run the picks step
Read what it prints: a checkpoint, or a warning that you ticked out of order
Once the cage PC is published, the shipped ones move to Already on production

entries.title: A What’s new button on staging, listing what the cage PC does not have yet
entries.summary: On the staging site only, a What’s new button opens this drawer and lists every change that is on staging and not yet on the cage PC, in the order it will ship. Anything already on the cage PC is tucked underneath.
watchFor: The cage PC site has no such button, and no hidden one either.
The list is re-read every time you open the drawer, so it always matches the build you are on.
howToSee: Open the staging site, not the cage PC site
Click What’s new beside Code Lookup
The changes list in the order they will ship
Open the cage PC site instead and there is no button at all

entries.title: What’s new cards you can skim, with a Tested tick
entries.summary: The What’s new cards now start closed, so you see the change and one line about it. Open one to read what changed, what to watch for and how to try it, and tick Tested once you have checked it.
watchFor: A ticked card drops to the bottom of the list and keeps a tick mark while it is closed.
The ticks are saved on this device only. They never travel in the Day Export and the cage PC never sees them.
The words on the cards are plainer now. The full engineering detail is still one click away on each change.
howToSee: Open What’s new on staging: every card is closed
Click a title to open one and read What changed, Watch for and Try it
Tick Tested on a card and watch it drop to the bottom
Reload the page, open the drawer again, and the tick is still there

entries.title: Write feedback on a What’s new card and send it back
entries.summary: Open a card on What’s new and there is now a box under Try it where you can write what you saw, saved on this device as you type. Copy all feedback puts every note on the clipboard, and if this browser holds a GitHub token each card also gets a Send to GitHub button that posts your note as a comment on that change.
watchFor: The Send button only appears when this browser already holds a GitHub token. Without one you still get Copy all feedback.
A card you have written on shows a small speech bubble in its header, and the top line counts how many have feedback.
Edit a note you already sent and the button re-arms, so you can send the new version.
The notes are saved on this device only. They never travel in the Day Export and the cage PC never sees them.
howToSee: Open What’s new on staging and click a card title to open it
Type something in the Feedback box under Try it
Close the card and look for the speech bubble beside the Tested tick
Click Copy all feedback and paste it somewhere to read it back

entries.title: Send to GitHub works from the work PC again
entries.summary: Send to GitHub was answering 401 on a token that was fine, because the tool was reading the saved token without unwrapping it. It now reads the token the same way it was saved.
watchFor: If Send still says 401, the token itself has expired. Save a fresh one in Settings.
The button only shows when a token is saved on that device.
howToSee: Open What’s new on the work PC and open a card
Type a note and click Send to GitHub
The line under the box reads Sent with a link to the comment

entries.title: Set a GitHub token for feedback, and failures that tell you what to do
entries.summary: Send to GitHub now has its own token, set from a GitHub token button in the drawer, so it does not have to borrow one from a sync channel that points at a different repo. When a send fails, the line under the box says what went wrong and what to do about it.
watchFor: A token scoped to another repo gets a 404, not a permission error. The message now says so.
The token is saved on this device only. It is never copied, exported, or shown again after you save it.
If no token is set, Send is hidden and Copy all feedback still works.
howToSee: Open What’s new and click GitHub token
Paste a token with Issues read and write on the work repo, and click Save
Send to GitHub appears on every card
Send a note and read the line under the box

entries.title: Pressing 33 or 65 no longer opens the package details
entries.summary: The 33 and 65 buttons, Apply and Done now code the row and nothing else. The row stays where it is, at the same height, so the next button is still under your finger and you can run straight down the list.
watchFor: The row still dims and shows Coded 33 with an Undo, the same as before.
Clicking anywhere else on the row — the name or address cell — still opens the details, on purpose.
If the row you code was showing its details, coding it closes them. Other rows you opened stay open.
howToSee: Load today's Inbound and Van Scans report
In Needs Manual Review, click the orange 33 on four rows in a row as fast as you can
No details panel opens under any of them and the list does not move
Click the address on the next row down: the details still open there

entries.title: The 503 button now moves the package to the 503s tab in one click
entries.summary: Clicking 503 on a Needs Manual Review row now tags it AND hands it off: the row leaves your list and shows up in the 503s tab right away. Typing 503 into Goes To works exactly as it did before — that row stays in your list until you barcode and confirm it.
watchFor: Only the package you clicked is handed off. Another package at the same stop still gets the 503 tag, but stays in your list for the barcode sheet.
Clear 503 on the tab row brings the package back to your list and takes the filing back with it.
In Work mode the cursor moves to the next row after the click, and that row’s street goes on the clipboard, the same way Park already works.
The tool sometimes refuses to set the area, when the report has no readable sort date or already confirmed that area. Nothing is filed and you see the refusal instead.
howToSee: Load today’s Post Sort report
Click 503 on a row in Needs Manual Review
Open Set aside and click 503s — the package is already there
Type 503 into another row’s Goes To instead: that one stays in the list
Click Clear 503 on the tab row and the first package comes back

entries.title: The page opens folded shut, and remembers what you opened
entries.summary: Every section now starts collapsed on every load, so a report lands as a short list of headers with counts instead of a wall of rows, and what you open is remembered across a refresh. The Collapse all and Expand all buttons moved up into the purple bar at the top, so they stay on screen no matter how far you scroll.
watchFor: A refresh used to open everything back up. It no longer does — only the sections you opened yourself come back.
A re-drop of today’s report keeps what you had open. A report from a new sort day starts with everything shut.
Every collapsed header still shows its count, so a folded page still tells you where the work is.
Work mode, unchanged: a load still opens the section holding the cursor, and on a Post Sort load all three buckets — so there the sections are remembered, the buckets are not.
howToSee: Drop a report — every section lands folded shut
Click a section header to open it
Press F5 — that section is open again and the rest are still shut
Use the Collapse all and Expand all buttons in the purple bar at the top of the page

entries.title: The production deploy refuses to run from the wrong branch
entries.summary: Sending the coder to the cage PC now stops unless the computer is on the release branch and that branch has been pushed. Deploys to the staging site are unchanged.
watchFor: A refused deploy leaves the live site exactly as it was. Nothing is built and nothing is copied, so there is no half-finished update to clean up.
Sitting on a detached commit is refused too, even when it is the exact tip of release. Check the release branch out first.
If the release branch has commits that were never pushed, the deploy stops and tells you to push them first.
The refusal names the branch you are on and the exact commands to fix it.
howToSee: Try a production deploy from a main checkout
Read the refusal: it names the branch you are on and what to run instead
Check out the release branch and run the same command again
The deploy runs as before and the live site updates

entries.title: The other desk's Goes To prints on the barcode card, and says if it is a guess
entries.summary: When the other desk types a Goes To, your printed card now shows that area instead of a dash. If they typed it on the post sort lane, the card carries the same unconfirmed line their own card carries.
watchFor: An area they typed on the post sort lane prints with the line reading unconfirmed, post sort early guess, not yet scanned. Their card says the same thing, so the two desks agree.
An area they answered against the full report prints plain, with no line. The line is about which report a value was typed against, not about who typed it.
Both desks must be on this build. An older one refuses the new file and shows a dash again, and tells you to update that device.
A row with no area, or an area that came from the report itself, still prints a dash on purpose.
howToSee: Load today's report on both desks and update both
On the other desk, type a Goes To on the post sort lane - say 140
Wait for your screen to pick it up; the box shows 140 with their name
Tick that row, click Barcode selected, and read the card: 140 with the unconfirmed line under it

entries.title: FTrack and E-OPS links beside every tracking number
entries.summary: The Station tab tracking number is now click-to-copy with an FTrack link beside it. E-OPS links now sit next to FTrack on 503s, Parked and Manually Resolved as well.
watchFor: E-OPS only appears on an Express package. A Ground row shows FTrack alone, which is right - there is no E-OPS entry to open for a Ground package.
Clicking either link never copies the tracking number and never opens the row. Click the number itself to copy it - on Full barcode it copies the scan barcode instead.
A station package the report has stopped carrying keeps both links, so you can still look it up while it sits in the cage.
Repeat History and the Recurring list still show FTrack alone. Neither one records whether a package was Express.
howToSee: Load the Inbound and Van Scans report
Open Set aside and click Station
Click a tracking number to copy it, then click FTrack beside it
Find an Express row in Needs Manual Review and check E-OPS sits next to FTrack

entries.title: To Station is now a button with an arrow for more moves
entries.summary: To Station still works with one click. The small arrow beside it opens a list with To Station, Mark as done, Park, 503 and Not ours, so a row can be moved without hunting for the right button.
watchFor: Each item does exactly what the button of that name does, including the 503 one, so nothing new is written and nothing behaves differently.
Park and 503 keep their own buttons in the row as well. Use whichever you already reach for.
On the last row of a long list the menu opens upward so the bottom item is never off the screen.
While the menu is open the arrow keys move inside it and do not step the work cursor. Press Escape to close it and the arrow goes back to the list.
howToSee: Load today's report and find a row in Needs Manual Review
Click the small arrow to the right of To Station
Pick Mark as done and watch the row move to the Work area assigned tab
Scroll to the last row and open the arrow again: the menu opens upward

entries.title: Back to the top, and jump straight to a section
entries.summary: A Top button now floats in the bottom left corner once you scroll, and the purple bar carries a chip for each section so you can jump straight to one.
watchFor: The button sits bottom left on purpose. Bottom right is where the day and night toggle lives, and where a row keeps its own buttons on the last line you can see.
The Home key takes you to the top and the End key to the bottom, but neither fires while you are typing in a code box or in the Goes To box.
On a phone the chips drop their counts and shrink, so the purple bar does not eat the screen.
A chip opens the section it jumps to, so a jump never lands on a folded section.
howToSee: Load today Inbound and Van Scans report
Scroll down into Ready to Enter until the Top button appears in the bottom left corner
Click a chip in the purple bar and watch that section land just under the bar
Press the Home key with nothing selected and the page goes back to the top

entries.title: Load New File empties the review list, and both reports load from the drop zone
entries.summary: After Load New File the empty Needs Manual Review box is gone and the drop zone offers both reports side by side. Set aside stays only while one of its tabs still holds packages.
watchFor: Set aside stays while any tab still holds packages. Station packages carry over from day to day, so on a real sort the strip is usually still there, counting what is left.
The park is never cleared. The parked tab reads zero while no report is loaded, because there is no row to draw yet, and the package is back the moment you load the next report.
Post Sort is the first tile because it takes the main slot. Once a report is loaded the drop zone stands down, so swap in a fresh pull from the review strip as before.
In dark mode the drop zone outline is light purple now. It used to be a faint grey a shade off the page and was easy to miss on an empty screen.
howToSee: Load today report and code a few rows
Click Load New File
Needs Manual Review is gone, and the drop zone with both loads is back
Park a row and click Load New File again: the parked tab reads zero, and the park itself is kept
Load a report and the parked package is counted again and ready to unpark

entries.title: An admin's 503 moves on your screen, and takes the stop with it
entries.summary: When an admin presses the 503 button the package leaves your Needs Manual Review and lands in your 503s tab, named for whoever pressed it. The press now files every package at that same address, not just the one they pressed.
watchFor: Only the 503 BUTTON does this. A 503 typed into the Goes To box still waits in your list until somebody marks it done.
Their row is read-only: it carries their name instead of a Clear 503. File it yourself and your own Clear 503 comes back.
A package YOU parked stays in Parked even if they mark it done. Unpark it and it drops into the 503s tab on the next pull.
Clear 503 on the package that was PRESSED brings the whole stop back. Clear on one of the others brings back only that one.
howToSee: Load today's report on both devices
On the admin device press 503 on a package at a stop that has two packages
On your device wait for the next desk pull
Both packages are gone from Needs Manual Review and are in Set aside > 503s, with their name on them
Have them type 503 into a different row instead: that one stays in your list

entries.title: FTrack opens the new site, and a quick Address chip for no-address rows
entries.summary: Every FTrack button, in every tool, now opens the new FTrack site. On your device you can also turn on an Address chip in Settings, which opens the FTrack delivery page with the address on rows with no street.
watchFor: The Address chip is off until you tick it in Settings, and only your device has the checkbox. The admins see only the FTrack chip, which still opens the full history.
It shows only on rows with no house number and street, the same rows Hide no-address counts. A row with a real address never gets one.
If FTrack opens a blank or error page, tell me. The history link reuses the old link's settings, which only the FedEx network can confirm.
howToSee: Load today's report and click FTrack on any row: it opens on ftrack.prod.cloud.fedex.com
Open Settings and tick Show the Address chip on no-address rows
Rows with no street now show Address next to FTrack, with no reload
Click Address: the FTrack delivery page opens in a new tab with the address
Untick the box and the chips go away

entries.title: New Writeups page drafts a Late Notice of Deficiency
entries.summary: A new Writeups page builds the Workday text for a Late. Pick the admin, type each Late from MyTime, tick the ones the writeup covers, and copy the Discipline Details and Next Steps boxes into Workday.
watchFor: Only Lates and the Notice of Deficiency so far. History, Final Notice, call-offs and the other kinds come in the next tickets.
Everything stays in this browser. Nothing is sent anywhere.
It has no Command Center tile yet. That comes with the deploy ticket.
howToSee: Open the Writeups page from the repo and add an admin
Add a Late with its date, scheduled start and clock-in
Tick it and read the two boxes on the right
Click Copy on a box and paste it somewhere

entries.title: Writeups drafts Call-offs and NCNS, shows the 30-day pattern, and adds a habitual toggle
entries.summary: The Writeups page now drafts Call-offs and no call no shows as well as Lates, and shows the last 30 days as counts against the house standard. A Document as habitual toggle switches the wording, and a note beside it says when the ticked incidents meet the standard.
watchFor: A Call-off ticked as Protected Sick Time is never put in the draft and never counted. The page says so under the toggle.
The habitual toggle starts off and goes back off whenever you tick or untick an incident. The note beside it never turns it on.
Only one Late, Call-off or NCNS is allowed per admin per day. Adding a second of any kind is refused.
howToSee: Open the Writeups page and pick an admin
Add a Call-off with Protected Sick Time ticked, then tick it in the list and see the draft stay empty
Add three Lates in the last 30 days, tick them, and read the note beside Document as habitual
Turn the toggle on and read "habitual tardiness" in Discipline Details

entries.title: Writeups keeps each admin's writeup history and suggests Notice or Final Notice
entries.summary: The Writeups page now keeps a history of each admin's writeups on this device and suggests the next document from it, with a one-line reason. Drafts list prior discipline from the last 12 months, Related Disciplinary Actions shows the most recent writeup, and Final Notice can be drafted.
watchFor: A writeup goes into history only when you press Save to history. Copying a box never saves it.
With a Final Notice in the last 12 months the page names termination as the next step under policy and picks no document type. You can still pick one.
Documented Discussions are listed as prior discipline but are not counted as Notices. A writeup exactly 12 months old no longer counts, so check that edge against Workday.
Save to history is refused when the ticked incidents are already in a saved writeup, under any type. To change the type, delete the saved writeup, then save again.
howToSee: Open the Writeups page and pick an admin with no saved writeups, and read the empty history message
Add a past Notice of Deficiency from Workday and see the suggestion change to the 2nd notice
Tick a Late, press Save to history, and see the suggestion move to Final Notice
Read the Prior discipline sentence at the end of Discipline Details

entries.title: Writeups boxes can be edited by hand, and the page checks the citation and the dates
entries.summary: You can now type in the draft boxes, and an edited box keeps your text until you press Reset on it. The check line warns about HMR-057, a date that is not a ticked incident, or Next Steps that do not fit the type, and Replace swaps in POLICY-010 while keeping every date and fact.
watchFor: An edited box no longer follows the ticked incidents. Press Reset on that box to rebuild it.
Hand edits are not saved. A reload, switching admin or Save to history throws them away.
In a Prior discipline sentence only the past writeup's own issued date is skipped. Every other date must be a ticked incident, and every ticked incident's date must be in the text.
The warnings never stop Copy or Save to history. Read them before you paste.
howToSee: Open the Writeups page, tick a Late, and type in Discipline Details
Tick another Late and see your text stay, then press Reset
Paste a sentence citing hmr-057 and press Replace with the POLICY-010 sentence
Change a date in the box and read the amber date warning

entries.title: Writeups drafts a Documented Discussion, including a pattern of sick early departures
entries.summary: Documented Discussion is now a document type, with its four Workday boxes and no Rating, for a Late, a Call-off, an NCNS or two or more sick early departures. A sick one states only the dates, times and time missed, and medical words in any writeup warn in amber.
watchFor: A sick early departure is never counted toward a pattern and never goes into a Notice or Final Notice. Ticked under a Notice it is left out with a message.
Sick early departures draft only into a Documented Discussion, two or more and nothing else ticked. A saved one is never prior discipline on another writeup.
Words like doctor, ER or appointment warn on any writeup. Words like because or family warn only when sick time is ticked. Appointment packages never warn.
Previous Counseling Given lists writeups from the last 12 months. With none it stays empty.
howToSee: Open the Writeups page, tick a Late, and pick Documented Discussion
Add two sick early departures with a scheduled end and a clock-out, then tick both
Pick Documented Discussion and read the facts-only text
Type doctor's note into a box and read the amber warning

entries.title: Writeups drafts a performance writeup from an instruction and the misses
entries.summary: The Writeups page has a Performance kind. Add the Instruction and a Miss for each time it was not done, tick them, and the page drafts a Notice, Final Notice or Documented Discussion with Reason Performance, still citing POLICY-010.
watchFor: Performance entries draft only on their own, with one Instruction and at least one Miss. Ticked beside a Late, Call-off or NCNS they are left out, and the page says so.
Type each Miss as the sentence it should read, such as Sam did not scan the packages. The page adds On and the date.
The draft never says insubordination. If the word is typed into an entry or a box, an amber warning names the box.
Next Steps says the admin is expected to do the instruction. Add every shift by hand if it is a standing one. Whether to cite POLICY-031 instead is still open with HR.
howToSee: Open the Writeups page, pick an admin, and choose Performance in the incident kind
Add an Instruction, then two Misses on later dates
Tick all three and read Discipline Details and Next Steps
Pick Documented Discussion and see the Rating row go away

entries.title: Writeups can export and import its history as a backup file
entries.summary: The Writeups page has a Backup panel. Export history saves every admin, incident and writeup to one dated file, and Import history loads one back, and the page nudges an export after each saved writeup.
watchFor: Import replaces everything on this device. Nothing is merged, so anything not in the file is gone. The page shows what the file holds and waits for you to confirm.
A file that is damaged, from another tool, from a newer version, or holds a writeup dated in the future is refused. Nothing on the device changes.
Export warns you if the file it saved would be refused on import, such as a Late and a Call-off on one day. Fix the record and export again.
The file holds real names and incidents. Keep it off shared drives and out of the repo.
howToSee: Open the Writeups page, add an admin, and add a past writeup under Writeup history
Read the amber note that history changed since your last export, then press Export history
See the note clear and Last exported show today, and find the dated backup file in Downloads
Press Import history, choose that file, and read the counts and export date before confirming

entries.title: Writeups has a tile on the Command Center and ships in the hosted build
entries.summary: The Command Center has a Writeups tile that opens the Writeups page. The hosted build now carries the page, without the admin roster, so on the hosted page you add your admins by hand once.
watchFor: The hosted page starts with no admins. Add them once and they stay in this browser.
The page has no names baked in on the hosted build. Your admins, incidents and history never leave your browser.
The hosted build only changes when it is deployed. Merging alone does not put the tile on the hosted site.
howToSee: Open the Command Center and find the Writeups tile next to NVS Builder
Click it and the Writeups page opens
On the hosted site, the admin list starts empty with a message to add one

entries.title: Writeups warns on more everyday medical spellings
entries.summary: The medical-words warning now also catches spellings like ob-gyn, ER visit, psychiatrist, chiropractor, ultrasound, diabetes, asthma, blood pressure, sore throat, quarantine, PCP and Rx.
watchFor: Cramps, contractions and specialist warn only when sick time is ticked, so an ordinary Late or NCNS writeup stays quiet.
PCP and Rx warn only in capitals.
howToSee: Open the Writeups page and tick a Late
Type ob-gyn into Discipline Details and read the amber warning

entries.title: Writeups adds the admin's work schedule to absence writeups
entries.summary: Each admin on the Writeups page can have scheduled days, checked once on the admin panel. Call-off, NCNS and sick pattern drafts then say "Sam's work schedule is Sun-Thu." right after the incident facts, and an amber warning appears when a checked absence falls on a day that is not scheduled.
watchFor: Scheduled days are optional and saved in this browser only. With none set, the draft has no schedule line and a quiet note says so. It is not a warning.
Late and Performance drafts never get the schedule line.
The off-schedule warning names the date and weekday. It never blocks Copy, so check the date and the days before pasting.
Export history keeps each admin's scheduled days. Backups made before this change still import.
howToSee: Open the Writeups page, pick an admin, and check the days they work on the admin panel
Add an NCNS, tick it, and read the work schedule sentence in Discipline Details
Add an NCNS on a day that is not checked and read the amber warning
Clear the days and see the schedule sentence go away and the quiet note appear

entries.title: Writeups gets a Settings panel for wording and word lists
entries.summary: A Settings panel at the bottom of the Writeups page lets you change the attendance expectation, the attendance and performance consequences, the Final Notice line and the work schedule line. You can also add medical words, station phrases that should not warn and Workday Reason values, raise the sick-pattern minimum, and keep your First name or "Admin" choice between visits.
watchFor: A sentence that cites HMR-057 or policy 057, holds a medical word, or drops {name} or {days} is refused with a message, and nothing is saved.
Medical words can only be added, and a station phrase cannot hold any medical or reason word, like "doctor office" or "sick time".
The attendance consequence must keep "30 days", and the sick-pattern minimum never goes below 2.
Unreadable saved Settings never block Export, and Reset settings puts the defaults back.
howToSee: Open the Writeups page and open Settings at the bottom of the left column
Change the attendance consequence, press Save, and tick an incident to see it in Next Steps
Press Reset to default and see the original sentence come back
Type HMR-057 into a sentence, press Save, and read the refusal

entries.title: One People list, edited in the browser, used by the Time-Off Log and Address Catcher
entries.summary: A new People page lists your admins and staff, with a People tile on the Command Center. Add, rename or remove someone there and the Time-Off Log's Admin suggestions and Address Catcher's "Made by" line follow.
watchFor: The list stays in this browser. Every tool on the same site reads it, but another device, or the hosted site at first, starts empty until you add people or use Import.
Each tool keeps its built-in list for what the People list lacks: the Time-Off Log until someone is an Admin, Address Catcher until someone has an employee ID.
Renaming an admin splits their Time-Off history, because entries are stored under the old name. The People page warns and asks you to confirm.
Mark admins as Admin, or they do not show in the Time-Off Log. A list that cannot be read is never saved over: replace it with a backup.
howToSee: Open the Command Center and click the People tile
Add a person, mark them Admin, and save
Open the Time-Off Log and type in the Admin field: the new name is suggested
Rename or remove the person on the People page and see the suggestion change

entries.title: Writeups page seeds and suggests admins from the People list
entries.summary: On a new device the Writeups admin list starts from the admins on your People list. Admins you add to People later show as one-click Add buttons under Add an admin, with an Edit people link.
watchFor: Nothing is added on its own after the first load. Click Add to bring someone in.
If the People list has no admins, the Writeups page starts from its built-in list as before.
Names already on the Writeups list keep their history. Nothing is renamed or removed.
howToSee: Open the People page and mark a new person as Admin
Open the Writeups page and look under Add an admin
Click the Add button for that person and see them in the Who is this writeup for list

entries.title: Hosted tools show their app icon and a tab icon
entries.summary: The hosted Command Center now ships its app icons, so the install and home screen icons show up instead of a blank tile. Every tool tab also shows its icon in the browser tab.
watchFor: Only the hosted site changes. The next Command Center deploy is what puts the icons online.
A phone that already installed the app may keep the old blank icon until it is added again.
howToSee: Open the hosted Command Center in a browser
Look at the browser tab and see the station icon
Open any tool from the Command Center and see the same icon on its tab
